Item Summary
..title
RFB No. 2026-0412-B for Building 059 - Fire Station No. 7 Re-Roof, Project No. FAC-F-00139, for the Engineering Department to Shoemake Holdings, Inc. DBA Premiere Roofing in the amount of $242,310; and authorizing the City Manager to execute all necessary documents.
..body
Background
The Engineering Department accepted bids on July 28, 2026 for the Fire Station No. 7 Re-Roof (Project Number FAC-F-00139).  The project includes roof replacement for Fire Station No. 7.

The lowest responsive and responsible bid was submitted by Shoemake Holdings, Inc. DBA Premiere Roofing in the amount of $242,310.  There were a total of 2,050 vendors notified of this project.  Twelve (12) complete bids were received for the project as shown in the attached bid recap.

If this project is not awarded, the existing roofing system will remain in service beyond its expected useful life resulting in higher maintenance costs and increased risk of failure over time.
Financial Summary/Strategic Goals
Funding for this item is budgeted in the 2026-27 Fire & Public Safety Facilities CIP.  Construction services for the Fire Station No. 7 Re-Roof project, in the total amount of $242,310, will leave a balance of $202,690 available for future expenditures.

Approval of this item will support the City's Strategic Plan Critical Success Factor of being an Excellent, Innovative, and Accountable City Government.

matters.title: To transfer the sum of $500,000 from the Recreation Center Renovations Fund Unappropriated fund balance to the Recreation Center Renovations Fund Operating Appropriation for fiscal year 2025-26 for the purchase and installation of a generator at the Tom Muehlenbeck Recreation Center, amending the Community Investment Program of the City adopted by Ordinance No. 2025-9-6, specifically Section 1, Item “A”, to reflect the actions taken herein; declaring this action to be in the public interest; and providing an effective date.

Item Summary
..title
To transfer the sum of $500,000 from the Recreation Center Renovations Fund Unappropriated fund balance to the Recreation Center Renovations Fund Operating Appropriation for fiscal year 2025-26 for the purchase and installation of a generator at the Tom Muehlenbeck Recreation Center, amending the Community Investment Program of the City adopted by Ordinance No. 2025-9-6, specifically Section 1, Item “A”, to reflect the actions taken herein; declaring this action to be in the public interest; and providing an effective date.
..body
Previous Action/Presentation
On September 8, 2025, City Council adopted the Community Investment Program Budget Ordinance for the 2025-26 fiscal year, which included appropriations for the Recreation Center Renovations Fund of $3,184,284.
Background
Supplemental appropriations have been approved in the past on an as-needed basis by the City Council to address funding requirements that were not identified within previously adopted budgets and would not be prudent to delay to the next fiscal year.

This agenda item would amend the current Recreation Center Renovations Fund (Fund 21) operating appropriation for the current year by granting an additional expenditure capacity of $500,000 that would otherwise be held within the fund balance of the Recreation Center Renovations Fund (Fund 21). In this case, additional interest earnings revenues received in the Recreation Center Renovations Fund (Fund 21) from the previous fiscal year, FY 2024-25, will be used to cover the one-time costs associated with the purchase and installation of a generator at the Tom Muehlenbeck Recreation Center.

This funding was not planned when the current budget was adopted.
Financial Summary/Strategic Goals
This is the first supplemental appropriation for the FY 2025-26 Recreation Center Renovations Fund (Fund 21) Budget, totaling $500,000.

Approving additional Recreation Center Renovations Fund (Fund 21) appropriations for the 2025-26 fiscal year for these one-time costs relates to the City’s Strategic Plan Critical Success Factor of Excellent, Innovative, and Accountable City Government.
